tasks.title: Capture the owned package rename reference universe
tasks.goal: Determine the complete authorized affected scope before editing any package coordinate.
steps: Add explicit rename intent distinguishing display label, owned coordinate, path move, spec-anchor rename and local alias; this capability implements the owned-coordinate case.
Capture editable package and selected consumers through authoritative manifest/dependency/choice/provider/spec-marker/resource-export/config/environment parsers.
Classify each reference as resolvable editable, generated, excluded foreign/history/outside scope or unknown/dynamic; ordinary Markdown/XML-data/opaque payload stays inert.
positive_cases: Affected environment definitions and declared code/spec references are included.
Outside consumers are reported as outside scope rather than assumed absent.
negative_cases: Foreign installed slots or historical receipts are treated as editable owned source.
Incomplete tree marker inventory claims whole-reference coverage.

tasks.title: Prepare exact rename edits and identity transitions
tasks.goal: Validate a reviewable semantic rename plan against captured saved-state inputs.
steps: Validate new coordinates/paths and build exact syntax-preserving authored edits/moves with before-images, old/new identity transitions and generated outputs to regenerate.
Resolve collisions, case/path aliases and mandatory unknown references before claiming complete compatibility; require expanded capture or explicit bounded incomplete disposition.
Apply the plan in memory to the same source world, re-resolve dependency/address graphs and generated projections, and expose the diff through shared prepare services.
positive_cases: An owned coordinate rename updates exact declared consumers while preserving comments and unrelated bytes.
A collision-free planned world re-resolves all mandatory in-scope references.
negative_cases: Substring replacement changes foreign prose, immutable evidence or a similarly named package.
An alias/redirect is silently invented to conceal missing references.

tasks.title: Apply rename with editor fencing and regeneration recovery
tasks.goal: Commit the prepared owned-source change through one writer and verify its regenerated post-state.
steps: Require saved recaptured inputs, ownership/lock/target generations and acknowledged M-16-D edit barrier; reserve operation identity before the first write.
Journal authored edits/moves with retained before-images, regenerate lock/boot/index from authored intent through existing engines, then re-resolve exact postconditions.
Expose status/events/recovery for every partial prefix; keep published identities, historical captures/receipts/signatures and deployed environments unchanged unless separately admitted.
positive_cases: A saved owned rename regenerates and navigates to the new coordinate consistently.
Interrupted multi-file rename recovers under exact before/after/third-state rules.
negative_cases: Dirty participant, lease expiry or disk drift is ignored during commit.
Runtime deployment/public registry is silently retargeted as part of source rename.
